steps.title: Test one repeat
steps.instruction: Build one example using the value shown. Run and inspect it.
steps.explain: ring has one value in this test. Follow how it controls the drawing before putting the commands in a loop.
steps.expected: One visible example from the group. Check its position, size, and color.
steps.question: Where is ring used in the drawing code?
steps.answer: Find the variable in the movement, size, or color expressions. A different value changes those instructions.
steps.help: Check the changed lines first. Keep parentheses and commas in place. Indent each line inside a loop or function by four spaces.

lines: r = 151 - ring * 10 + 6 * math.sin(5 * t + ring * 0.3) + 3 * math.cos(9 * t)

steps.title: Try 4 repeats
steps.instruction: Put the tested example in a loop. Use a short part of the input list first.
steps.explain: list(...) makes the repeat values available as a list. The slice [: 4] takes its first 4 values. The indented body runs once per value.
steps.expected: A partial group. Inspect the spacing and repeated shape before drawing all of them.
steps.question: Which part of the code changes how many examples are drawn?
steps.answer: The values supplied to the loop. The drawing instructions inside it stay the same.

steps.title: Repeat the whole group
steps.instruction: Replace the trial examples with this loop. Run the whole program again.
steps.explain: for ring in range(13): takes one value at a time. Indent the repeated body four spaces. The first line after the loop returns to the left edge.
steps.expected: The complete group. Compare it with the first example you tested.
steps.question: What changes if the loop has fewer values?
steps.answer: The body runs fewer times. range(n) supplies n values, starting at 0.
